Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

Title: Diagnosis
Details: The issue report indicates that the union operation in the XPath implementation does not sort nodes in document order in the resulting node-set. According to the XPath specification, when converting a node-set to a string, the string-value of the first node in document order should be returned. The failing test case involves an XPath expression with a union of two node sets (/vendor[1]/contact[4] | /vendor[1]/contact[1]) which expectations that the first node in document order is used. 

Inspection of the DOMNodePointer.getValue() and stringValue(Node) methods shows how the string values of nodes are computed by recursively concatenating string values of child nodes, but these methods do not address node ordering in a node-set.

The TreeCompiler.union(java.lang.Object[]) method returns a CoreOperationUnion operation initialized with the argument expressions, but presumably does not itself sort nodes. Because the union operation is composed using CoreOperationUnion, the problem likely lies within the CoreOperationUnion implementation that does not perform sorting of nodes in document order after the union operation.

This lack of sorting leads to returning the string value of the incorrect node (a node that is not the first in document order) when calling string(...) on the union node-set.

The evidence together points to CoreOperationUnion as the place where union results should be consolidated and sorted according to document order, and the absence of such sorting causes the failing test and issue.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
